lens: Real-time copilot rail (Gong/Balto-style): live cue cards, objection alerts and talk-track progress beside the call
name: Copilot Rail Studio
one_liner: A dark live-call cockpit with a real-time copilot rail beside the transcript, a faceted library of 200+ personas, and a guided AI persona wizard, built on shadcn/ui, Geist and OpenAI models.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the lens: the copilot rail is the centrepiece of the live call, and the library and wizard feed it. Two deliberate changes. (1) Mobbin returned no true live-coaching screens for these searches, so the rail is grounded in competitor write-ups (Aircall, Avoma, SalesGhost) and Descript's side-rail suggestion cards, not screenshots. (2) Briefing and debrief use checklist and evidence patterns instead of a rail, because a rail only earns its space mid-call. Self-scores (1-10): A 8, B 8, C 8, D 7.0, E 6.5, F1 6, F2 7, F3 3 (on F3, 3 means worth building).

design_language.typography: Geist Sans: headings 600 (H1 32/38, -0.02em tracking), body 15/24, 16/24 on mobile. Geist Mono 500 for timers, scores, weights and model IDs, with tabular numerals wherever a number moves. Sora is dropped.
design_language.shape_and_depth: 12px card radius, 8px controls, full pills for chips. Hairline borders carry structure; shadows only on floating sheets. The rail is a flat panel with a 2px accent in the cue's colour. The blurred orb is removed.
design_language.motion: Cue cards enter in 200ms (8px rise and fade), at most three visible. Score numbers roll in 400ms. Stepper checks draw in 300ms. The debrief ring tweens once over 600ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion, movement stops and colour changes remain.
design_language.iconography: Lucide at 1.75 stroke: 20px in the rail, 16px in chips. Cue types: shield-alert (objection), circle-help (next question), ear (whisper), flag (guardrail). Every colour state also has an icon and a text label, so colour is never the only signal.
design_language.theme_modes: Light is the default for library, briefing, debrief, dashboard and team. The live call and mobile live call default to the dark stage. Both follow prefers-color-scheme with a header toggle, and every colour is a :root token with dark overrides.

navigation_and_ia: Top bar: logo, Practice, Library, Progress, Team (role-gated), a Cmd-K button, theme toggle, account. Core path: Library (or Wizard), then Briefing, Live call, Debrief, Progress. Scenario choice moves from a dropdown into the library. The wizard is reachable from the library's New persona button, from an empty library, and from onboarding. On mobile, a bottom tab bar holds Practice, Library, Progress and More.

screens.layout: 390px. Top bar: persona avatar ring, name, mono timer, End and grade icon. Stage: the last two transcript turns, scrollable above. A cue card docks above the composer with one cue, 'Use line' and dismiss. The copilot rail becomes a bottom sheet with three snap points: peek (score and current step), half and full. Composer: 48px input, large mic button, send and pause. End and grade is a full-width bottom button behind a confirm sheet. Safe-area padding throughout.
screens.key_components: Compact header; two-turn transcript; docked cue card; bottom-sheet rail with three snap points; large mic button; confirm sheet; safe-area insets.
screens.change_vs_today: Today the talk track hides behind an icon and the floating dev badge overlaps the timer. The rail moves into a sheet, so coaching is one tap away without covering the call.

live_coaching_and_scoring: A separate coach channel. After each rep turn (debounced, one cue per turn, 8-second cooldown), a text model sees the last six turns, the rubric and the talk-track state, and returns schema-checked cues: objection, next question, whisper or guardrail, each citing a turn and a rubric criterion. The persona never sees cue text. Live scores use weighted partial credit per criterion, shown with deltas and the quote that earned them, labelled 'Live estimate'. The final grade comes from a full-transcript structured-output pass; if that fails, a visible heuristic chip and a re-grade button appear. Whisper is text only, so no audio bleeds into the mic. Self-score D 7.0, provided p50 cue latency stays under about 2 seconds and cue precision passes 30 scripted calls.
persona_library_and_wizard: Library: 200+ personas at launch across about 18 job families, each a JSON pack holding the persona, talk track, objection bank and rubric. Facets: role, industry, difficulty, objection type, call type and pack source. Community packs are labelled and pass the same schema check in CI. Wizard: five steps. Context sources are a job description, a product URL (fetched through an allowlist with size and time caps), CRM notes, ICP text, or a pasted call. Output is schema-validated, editable, dry-run tested, and saved privately or exported as a pack PR. Self-score E 6.5: the ceiling is content quality and review capacity, not the UI.
signature_moments: A cue appears in the rail as the objection lands, and 'Use line' drops the exact phrase into the composer for the rep to send. Nothing is auto-sent.
The talk-track stepper ticks live, so the rep sees progress without reading a checklist.
The debrief's 'Retry from turn 8' branches the call from the missed objection, turning the grade into practice.
Clicking any evidence chip highlights the exact transcript line that earned or lost points.
The wizard shows the JSON pack beside the form, so a generated persona is one PR away from the community library.
The landing hero plays a short split-screen loop of the rail reacting, with a static poster for reduced motion.
openai_fund_angle: Every OpenAI model has a visible job. 'Voice: gpt-realtime' sits on the live stage, 'Coach: gpt-4.1-mini' in the rail footer, 'Graded: gpt-4.1-mini, structured output' on each debrief, and 'Generated with' on each wizard persona. A Models page lists which model runs which job and accepts any OpenAI-compatible base URL. A Contributors page offers a copyable Codex CLI prompt that scaffolds a persona pack from the schema and opens a PR, with persona gaps labelled by job family as good first issues. API credits would pay for voice sessions, grading and wizard runs. Claim Codex maintainer use only if it is true for this repo.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 1 (S): tokens, Geist, shadcn primitives on existing screens, Tailwind v4 migration, and a fix for the mobile call layout. Phase 2 (M): copilot rail behind a feature flag, text mode first. Phase 3 (M): persona packs as JSON, faceted library, seed 200 personas. Phase 4 (M): wizard with export-as-PR. Phase 5 (M): debrief replay, progress and team views. Ship phases 1-3 for the fund application; the team view can slip.

risks: Coach latency or false cues turn the rail into a distraction. Mitigate with a cooldown, a cue cap, an Off mode and a measured p50 target.
Live scores can mislead on short calls. Always label them as estimates and gate the Met goal chip on full grading.
Persona content quality and licensing: 200 personas need review. Use a CONTRIBUTING rubric and a schema check in CI.
The wizard fetches URLs, which creates SSRF risk. Needs an allowlist, timeouts, size caps and a block on internal addresses.
Nine screens plus a rail and a wizard is a large surface for a volunteer-maintained repo. Phase it, and cut the team view first if needed.
Voice runs on ElevenLabs Agents today. The OpenAI Realtime path must be a working alternative, not a claim in the README.
shadcn copy-in means the repo owns the component code. Keep the Tailwind v4 migration out of the critical path.
Colour-coded cues need icons and labels for colour-blind users. The rail must also work at 1280px wide without squeezing the transcript below about 480px.
